text:
emma: quick thread — noticed a p99 spike on the canary for 13B during a short burst. looks like prefill is the noisy component this time, not decode. putting profiling snippets and hypotheses below.

raj: ok can you paste the numbers?

emma: TL;DR numbers from the sampling window (burst ~500r/s, seq len ~48 avg):
- prefill p50/p95/p99 = 42ms / 95ms / 480ms
- decode p50/p95/p99 = 110ms / 125ms / 420ms
- baseline (non-burst) prefill p99 ~210ms so the canary doubled prefill p99

emma: profiler dump (simplified):
```
prefill: 60% compute, 30% kernel-switch, 10% KV-warm
decode: 78% compute, 12% kernel-switch, 10% io
kernel chosen on path: quantized-4bit-fallback for many microbatches (heuristic tripped)
KV misses spiking during prefills: kv-miss-rate +3.2x vs baseline
```

tess: interesting — kernel-switch time up suggests our heuristic that picks quant path when implicit batch > 6 is misfiring under burst microbatch dynamics. were microbatch sizes larger during canary?

emma: yes. observed microbatch size distribution shifted: median microbatch=5 -> 9 during the tail of the burst. scheduler aggregated more requests per exec to keep throughput.

oliver: that could push the per-device occupancy into a regime where the quant path wins throughput but adds micro-penalties on prefill (kv layout + copy). also quant path kernel currently reads KV in different tile order which hurts warm cache locality.

raj: hypothesis list: 
1) microbatching heuristic increases microbatch size for short seq burst -> kernel selection flips -> prefill implementation for quant path has worse KV locality -> p99 regression.
2) KV cache alignment: sharded KV rows cause thrash when multiple concurrent prefills hit different shards at same time.
3) the splitpoint/scheduler is delaying prefill execution so prefill work is queued behind decode-heavy jobs, creating head-of-line spikes.

emma: proposed quick experiments (canary-safe):
- A) force kernel override to fp16 path for the canary for 2 hours and measure p95/p99 (tess)
- B) cap microbatch size to 6 for prefill-only scheduling and compare tail latency (oliver)
- C) enable KV-prefetching for hot keys in runtime via small heuristic for 1% traffic (perf-bot record)
- D) add finer-grained per-request tagging to trace which shard a prefills touches (low-risks)

tess: started A now on canary pool-3. I'll flip after 30min sample.

perf-bot: experiment A deployed to pool-3 @2419876600 — kernel override fp16 enabled (rollout 10%). Monitoring p50/p95/p99.

emma: quick results after ~25min:
- kernel override sample (10%): prefill p99 -> 290ms (from 480ms)
- decode p99 in same sample -> 430ms (small regression ~+10ms)
notes: throughput unchanged, CPU-side scheduling unchanged.

raj: override helps prefill tails a lot but decode got slightly worse. suggests quant path was partially helping decode throughput; we traded some decode perf for prefill stability.

oliver: that matches the occupancy theory. next we should try B (microbatch cap) to see if we can keep quant path but avoid large microbatches that flip kernel heuristics. I'm taking B.

tess: B started — capping microbatch to 6 for prefill eligible queues, rollout 20% to canary pools @2419876700.

perf-bot: experiment B deployed @2419876705 — microbatch cap=6 (20% rollout). Collecting 10min windows.

tess: early B observations: prefill p99 -> 320ms, decode p99 -> 415ms. So better than baseline for prefill, smaller impact on decode vs A.

emma: promising. microbatch cap seems to be a good middle ground. But KV misses still slightly elevated. we still need to tackle KV alignment/locking.

oliver: for KV alignment I can prototype a per-shard warmup that preloads KV rows for hot prefixes. low-risk; run on 1% traffic. will need a small runtime flag to enable prefetch.

raj: operational checklist before broader rollouts:
- metric dashboards: show prefill vs decode separate p50/p95/p99 over rollout buckets
- kernel-selection feature flag to allow per-model override
- microbatching cap as tunable policy per-route
- KV-prefetch flag and a landing PR with perf regression tests

emma: action items:
- tess: keep A running (revert if decode regression >10%). capture 1h window metrics.
- tess/oliver: finish B 30min run and post the raw histograms.
- oliver: prototype KV-prefetch PoC and perf harness (start 1% traffic).
- raj: update SLO doc to include prefill vs decode tail budgets and a note about kernel-selection heuristics.

tess: noted. uploading sample histograms in a follow-up msg.

oliver: I'll also add a small profiler trace with tile-order counters so we can confirm the KV access pattern difference between kernels.

emma: thanks all. next sync if any experiment flips major metrics. if B holds, we can consider microbatch cap as default for mixed burst workloads and then iterate on KV prefetch + kernel micro-optimizations. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: summary metrics snapshot posted to /ml/perf/reports/2419876543/canary-summary at 2419876790
